collection_summary: Factual-lookup instance recording the EU accession year for each of the 27 current EU member states per Wikidata. Universe is the set of countries with `P463=Q458` (member of: European Union) and no `P582` end-time qualifier — exactly the 27 current members. Accession year is the `P580` start-time qualifier on the P463 statement, projected to year precision. Claim type is `source_defined` rather than `exhaustive` because the natural-language question 'in what year did each EU member join' has multiple defensible answers per founding member (1957 Treaty signed vs. 1958 Treaty in force vs. 1993 Maastricht / EU per se), and this instance commits to Wikidata's specific per-country convention. Result: 27 rows × 2 columns, sorted by accession year then country.
source_coverage_notes: Single-source instance grounded entirely in the Wikidata SPARQL endpoint. The 27-row count matches the well-known current EU membership and is independently verifiable against Wikipedia's 'Enlargement of the European Union' article. Year distribution matches the standard enlargement waves: 6 founders in 1957–58, then 1973 (Denmark, Ireland), 1981 (Greece), 1986 (Portugal, Spain), 1995 (Austria, Finland, Sweden), 2004 (10 countries — Cyprus, Czech Republic, Estonia, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, Slovakia, Slovenia), 2007 (Bulgaria, Romania), 2013 (Croatia). The UK is correctly excluded via the P582 end-time filter post-Brexit.
decision_log: 1) Chose query_category=factual_lookup because the query is point-recall per entity — for each known member, a single attribute (year) is looked up. The category's stress is pure parametric recall, not decomposition or scope reasoning, which is exactly what this instance tests. 2) Chose operation_type='projection' to match the curation UI validator's accepted pairing (factual_lookup → projection). The query shape — universe given, single attribute returned per row — is a multi-row projection of one attribute. The membership-status filter is part of universe definition, not the dominant operation. (An earlier draft used 'filter' here; corrected after audit feedback that the validator rejects factual_lookup → filter.) 3) Used the statement-node form (p:P463/ps:P463 + pq:P580 + pq:P582) rather than the truthy shortcut `wdt:P463`, because reading qualifiers (start time, end time) requires the full statement node — `wdt:` strips qualifiers. 4) Used the safer SPARQL pattern from `references/sparql-gotchas.md` §1 Option B by explicitly excluding deprecated-rank statements (`FILTER NOT EXISTS wikibase:rank wikibase:DeprecatedRank`). Audit verified the 27-row count is identical with or without this filter for the current Wikidata snapshot, but the explicit exclusion is the documented safer default. 5) Excluded the UK via `FILTER NOT EXISTS pq:P582` rather than via rank filtering; Wikidata records UK's P463=Q458 statement with P582=2020-01-31 (Brexit), which the filter cleanly catches. 6) Did NOT manually unify the founders' accession year to a single value (1957 vs 1958). Wikidata records France, Italy, Belgium, Luxembourg, and Netherlands at 1957 (Treaty of Rome signed March 25, 1957) and Germany at 1958 (Treaty in force January 1, 1958). The 1957/1958 split represents the same legal event recorded with two date conventions in Wikidata. Per the curation hard rules, ground truth must trace to the cited source — manually unifying the values would be parametric-knowledge generation. 7) Set claim_type='source_defined' rather than 'exhaustive' because the natural-language question allows multiple defensible answers per founder (1957 / 1958 / 1993), and this instance commits to Wikidata's specific per-country convention. An 'exhaustive' claim would assert that every current EU member is listed and that the accession year for each is THE objectively correct one — the first half is true (universe is closed-world per Wikidata), but the second half is not (the year depends on which date convention you accept). 'source_defined' honestly reflects this scope.
normalization_decisions: Country names use the Wikidata English label as returned by the wikibase:label service; this preserves canonical forms such as 'Czech Republic' (not 'Czechia') and 'Germany' (not 'Federal Republic of Germany'). Years are bare integers (e.g., 2013, not '2013-07-01' and not '2013-07') per the protocol §6 date convention for year-only dates; the underlying P580 values are full ISO dates but the SPARQL `YEAR()` function projects them to year precision. Sort order is (accession year ASC, country ASC) — this groups co-acceding waves visually and is stable across reruns. Single-column primary key on Country is sufficient because each current member has exactly one current P463=Q458 statement; if Wikidata ever recorded multiple current memberships for one country (which would be a data error, not a real situation), the row would conflict on PK and surface immediately.
open_questions: 1) The founders' accession year split (1957 for 5 of 6, 1958 for Germany) is a Wikidata data-convention inconsistency — same event, different chosen dates per country article. Standard references (Wikipedia 'Enlargement of the European Union') typically use 1958 for all 6 founders (when the Treaty of Rome entered into force). An LLM under test might give 1957, 1958, or 1993 (Maastricht / EU per se) for any founder, and only the specific Wikidata-recorded year scores as correct. This is the main reason the claim_type is `source_defined` rather than `exhaustive`. 2) Whether to count membership in the EU's predecessor organizations (ECSC 1951, EEC 1957/58) as 'joining the EU' is a definitional choice. Wikidata answers 'no' (P463=Q458 specifically; ECSC and EEC are separate Q-items). The query phrasing 'join the European Union' aligns with that narrow reading. 3) The benchmark target for factual_lookup is 3 instances; this is the first. Future siblings could test other crisp date-recall facts (e.g., NATO accession years, ASEAN accession years) to round out the category without conceptual overlap. 4) If a future EU expansion or contraction occurs (Albania, Moldova, Ukraine, etc. acceding, or another departure), this instance's row count will change. The temporal_note records the access date so the snapshot is unambiguous. 5) The artifact-contract operation-type vocabulary table does not currently list factual_lookup → projection as an expected pairing; the UI validator does accept it. A future Track-2-style update to `references/artifact-contract.md` should add this row to the expected pairings table to prevent the next labeler from guessing wrong.
